A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same FMA research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original FMA classification, transfer, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, generalization experiments, and component ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 substantively revises a central training component. V3 uses feature-dependent Gaussian augmentation with target (z_c−x_hat_t)/(1−t); v4 uses x_hat_t=x_t+λt(1−t)ε with target z_c−x_0+λ(1−2t)ε. Both the augmented input distribution and regression target change. Appendix B nevertheless retains the old sampler, leaving the implementation behind the reported results unresolved.

E1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same 11 image-classification benchmarks and ImageNet-to-ten-target-dataset transfer scenario. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains CoOp, CoCoOp, TIP-Adapter, CLIP-Adapter, PLOT++, KgCoOp, ProGrad, and CLIP-LoRA. The corresponding comparator sets in Tables 1, 3, and 7 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented experiments retain their shot counts, splits, backbones, 200-epoch budget, AdamW learning rate, and validation-based inference-step selection. Section 3.2 revises the proposed training rule, but no separate change to the evaluation design or experimental settings is reported.

E4.justification: Figures 5–6 retain the same trajectory case study and analyses of backbones, inference strategies, and noise augmentation. No analysis comparing the earlier and revised augmentation rules is added.

E5.justification: Appendix C already reports standard deviations in Table 4 and p-values in Table 5 in v3. V4 retains these reporting practices and adds no run counts, seeds, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and the plotted empirical results are unchanged. For example, Tables 2–3 retain 16-shot CLIP-LoRA+FMA average accuracies of 77.8 and 88.8 for difficult and easy datasets. No separately reported results accompany the revised training formulation.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the formal noise-path definition in Eq. (4) and introduces its time derivative as Eq. (5), replacing the previous endpoint-directed velocity expression. The propositions, assumptions, and proofs in Section 4 and Appendix A otherwise remain unchanged apart from equation renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about one-step PEFT limitations, model-agnostic multi-step alignment, and particular benefits on difficult datasets.

C2.justification: The rationales for coupling, noise augmentation, and early stopping remain unchanged, as do the interpretation of generalization results and the future-work qualification concerning sample-specific stopping.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly defines the feature statistics controlling noise magnitude. V4 removes those definitions and introduces standard Gaussian ε and a noise-strength hyperparameter λ, without specifying its value or selection rule. Appendix B still uses the old σ²(x_t) sampler. Other implementation settings and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. The relationship to existing PEFT methods, flow matching, and Schrödinger-bridge work retains the same positioning and citations.

P1.justification: The noise-augmentation explanation receives a limited rewrite, replacing feature-statistic definitions with explanations of λ, ε, and the derivative target. The arXiv version/date and equation references are updated; the section structure and remaining prose are retained.

P2.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the inline velocity expression with a separately numbered displayed equation and locally reflows the surrounding material. All six figures and seven tables retain their placement, captions, and structure.

improvement.justification: V4 makes the revised noise path and velocity target mathematically consistent through Eqs. (4)–(5). However, Appendix B retains the conflicting v3 sampler, the new λ has no reported setting, and the unchanged experiments do not establish which formulation produced their results. The mathematical benefit and newly introduced reproducibility ambiguities prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
